newsitem.title: USA: Revco results higher excluding acquisition charge.
newsitem.headline: Revco results higher excluding acquisition charge.

text.p: Revco D.S. Inc. said Friday earnings for its latest quarter rose almost 19 percent before accounting for the acquisition of Big B Inc., an Alabama-based chain of drug stores.
Revco had net earnings for the fiscal 1997 third quarter, which ended Feb. 8, of $11.4 million, or 17 cents a share, including a non-recurring charge associated with the Big B acquisition.
Excluding the charge, Revco earned $30 million, or 44 cents a share, up 18.9 percent from the year-ago quarter's $24.7 million, or 37 cents a share.
Sales, aided by the acquisition of Big B, Inc., advanced 23.7 percent to $1.54 billion from $1.24 billion.
Through the end of the third quarter, Revco opened 97 stores, 48 of which were relocations and 16 were acquired stores. It closed 26 stores.
Revco has over 2,500 stores in 17 Midwestern, Southeastern and Eastern states.
Revco's comparable store sales increased "a very respectable 8 percent," said D. Dwayne Hoven, Revco president and chief executive officer.
"Net income was on plan and we maintained our integration schedule for the Big B acquisition," he said in a statement.
Revco stock was down 37.5 cents at $40.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
